title: Mary and Martha part 1
scripture_text: ’’As Jesus and his disciples were on their way, he came to a village where a woman named Martha opened her home to him. She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to what he said. But Martha was distracted by all the preparations that had to be made. She came to him and asked, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to do the work by myself? Tell her to help me!” “Martha, Martha,”the Lord answered, “you are worried and upset about many things, but few things are needed—or indeed only one. Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her.”
devotional:
The heart behind the service

We want to look at a well-known story about two sisters, and the different ways they responded to Jesus. In reading this story it is very easy to go down the lines of identifying with one of the sisters. Some feel that they can identify more with Martha than with Mary, these people would see themselves as being practical, they are the kind of people who are not afraid to get their hands dirty, they are eager to respond to the practical needs of others. However there are others like Mary, who is more devotional than practical, they are deep thinkers; people who like to sit at Jesus’ feet, they like to read and hold theological discussions. However, to approach the text in this way is to miss the point. Luke is not trying to set up one kind of service against another. The issue that Luke is addressing is much deeper than the type of service we offer; rather he is addressing the heart behind the service.

The initial welcome

‘As Jesus and his disciples went on their way, he came to a certain village where a woman named Martha opened her house to him.’

As we begin to look at this incident we need to remember that in bible times, hospitality was very important. In the ancient world the practice of hospitality meant to graciously receive a stranger into one's land, home, or community and provide directly for that person's needs. In the ancient world hospitality was nothing like today’s image of good hospitality. Because people travelled by foot, journeys took a long time, therefore travellers depended on the hospitality of others to help them on their way. Middle Eastern hospitality would have included the offering of a meal consisting of a number of different dishes from which guests could select. To share food with someone was to share life. So this was a very important time for the two sisters.

Luke tells us Martha opened her house to him. Martha wanted to show Jesus complete acceptance. Everything in her wanted to be a perfect host. (It is interesting that the name Martha means lady or mistress, she was the mistress or lady of the house;) she had a reputation to live up to, and cultural expectations to fulfil.

Often when we have a desire to do something for the Lord, everything with in us wants to do it right, we want to please him, but often we become like Martha, and we end up treating Jesus in the same way a bad host would mistreat an honoured guest. The things that were going on in Martha’s heart robbed Jesus of the hospitality He should have received. In serving God, the condition of our hearts is much more important than what we may be doing or any success we may have.

Martha’s mistakes

Martha is the predominate character in this incident, it is written so we can learn from her. Luke records not so much as one word spoken by Mary. She is like the silent observer.

Luke tells us more about what was going on inside Martha than what she was doing. ‘Martha was distracted.’ The word translated "distracted" is Greek perispao, from which we get our English word perspective, the word means ‘to be pulled in many directions or dragging a burden.' Martha’s mind and emotions were all over the place. The word was also used for a woman with a sad expression on her face. She was too preoccupied with being a good host and this was leading to an attitude that was entirely unhelpful. At this point Martha was loosing perspective. The things that she was doing had begun to take control of her. Her duties had begun to dictate her feelings, affections and thoughts toward herself and others.

Before we leave this point we should mention that sometimes people use their service for Jesus as a form of avoidance mechanism, they don’t want to deal with the issues of their own hearts, so they mistakenly think that if they are busy serving Jesus they must be okay. What we do for Jesus will mean very little to him, if anything, if we are refusing to face up to and deal with the issues that are going on inside us.
prayer: Father thank you that both Mary’s and Martha’s service was important to you
